title: Maize (Batar)
summary: Maize is the main staple crop of Timor-Leste, grown mostly in the wet season on rain-fed land.
actions: Plant at the start of the wet season (November–December) after the first good rains.
Space rows about 75 cm apart with 25 cm between plants; 2 seeds per hole, thin to 1.
Weed at 2 and 5 weeks after emergence — early weeds cause the biggest yield loss.
Top-dress with nitrogen (compost, manure tea or urea) when plants are knee high.
Harvest when husks are dry and kernels are hard, usually 90–120 days after planting.
Dry cobs well before storage; use sealed drums or bags to stop weevils.

sections.heading: Varieties
sections.body: Sele and Noi Mutin are improved open-pollinated varieties released in Timor-Leste with higher yield than local types. Keep seed from healthy, well-filled cobs for next season.

sections.heading: Planting
sections.body: Plant at the start of the wet season after the first good rains. Space rows 75 cm apart and plants 25 cm apart. Plant 2 seeds per hole and thin to the strongest plant.

sections.heading: Care
sections.body: Weed at 2 and 5 weeks. Top-dress with compost or nitrogen when plants reach knee height. Watch for fall armyworm in the whorl during the first 6 weeks.

sections.heading: Harvest and storage
sections.body: Harvest when husks are dry and kernels are hard. Dry cobs fully before storing in sealed drums to prevent weevil damage.

title: Rice (Hare)
summary: Lowland rice is grown in irrigated or rain-fed paddies; nursery seedlings are transplanted into level, flooded fields.
actions: Sow pre-soaked seed in a level, well-drained nursery bed 3–4 weeks before transplanting.
Transplant seedlings at 20–25 days, 2–3 seedlings per hill, 20 cm × 20 cm spacing.
Keep fields level so water depth is even (3–5 cm during tillering).
Drain the field for a few days at maximum tillering to strengthen roots.
Drain fully 1–2 weeks before harvest.
Harvest when 80–85% of grains are golden yellow.

sections.heading: Nursery
sections.body: Soak seed for 24 hours, drain for 24 hours, then sow in a raised, level nursery bed. Keep the bed moist, not flooded, for the first week.

sections.heading: Transplanting
sections.body: Transplant at 20–25 days. Plant 2–3 seedlings per hill at 20 × 20 cm. Shallow planting (2–3 cm) gives faster tillering.

sections.heading: Water
sections.body: Maintain 3–5 cm of water during tillering. Drain briefly at maximum tillering, then keep water until 1–2 weeks before harvest.

sections.heading: Harvest
sections.body: Harvest when 80–85% of the panicle is golden. Dry grain to 14% moisture before storage.

title: Tomato (Tomate)
summary: Tomato is a valuable vegetable crop best grown in the drier months; it is sensitive to fungal disease in humid weather.
actions: Raise seedlings in trays or a nursery bed; transplant at 3–4 weeks.
Space plants 50 cm apart in rows 70–100 cm apart.
Stake or trellis plants and remove lower leaves to keep air moving.
Water at the base in the morning; never wet the leaves.
Mulch with dry grass to keep soil moist and stop soil splashing onto leaves.
Rotate: do not plant tomato, chili or potato in the same bed two seasons in a row.

sections.heading: Planting
sections.body: Sow in trays and transplant at 3–4 weeks. Space 50 cm in the row and 70–100 cm between rows. The dry season (May–October) with irrigation gives the healthiest crop.

sections.heading: Care
sections.body: Stake plants, remove suckers and lower leaves, and mulch. Water at the base early in the morning. Feed with compost every 2–3 weeks.

sections.heading: Harvest
sections.body: Pick fruit when it starts to colour; it will ripen fully off the plant. Harvest every 2–3 days to keep plants producing.

title: Chili (Ai-manas)
summary: Chili is a high-value crop that tolerates heat well but needs good drainage and regular harvesting.
actions: Transplant seedlings at 4–6 weeks, 40–50 cm apart.
Plant on raised beds for drainage.
Mulch and water regularly; flowers drop if the plant dries out.
Harvest ripe fruit every few days to encourage more flowering.
Remove and destroy fruit with dark sunken spots (anthracnose).

sections.heading: Planting
sections.body: Raise seedlings for 4–6 weeks, then transplant 40–50 cm apart on raised beds. Chili likes full sun and well-drained soil.

sections.heading: Care
sections.body: Water regularly but avoid waterlogging. Mulch to keep moisture even. Feed with compost monthly.

sections.heading: Harvest
sections.body: Pick fruit when fully coloured. Regular picking keeps the plant productive for many months.

title: Beans (Fore)
summary: Common beans and cowpeas fix nitrogen, improve soil and are an excellent rotation crop after maize.
actions: Plant directly in the field, 2 seeds per hole, 30 cm apart in rows 50 cm apart.
Do not over-fertilise with nitrogen; beans make their own.
Intercrop with maize or plant after maize to restore soil fertility.
Harvest green pods young, or leave to dry fully for seed.

sections.heading: Why grow beans
sections.body: Beans fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, so the crop that follows (usually maize) grows better. They also mature quickly, in 60–90 days.

sections.heading: Planting
sections.body: Sow directly, 30 cm apart in rows 50 cm apart. Beans can be intercropped between maize rows.

sections.heading: Harvest
sections.body: Pick green pods young for eating. For dry beans, let pods dry on the plant, then shell and sun-dry the seed.

title: Cassava (Ai-farina)
summary: Cassava is a hardy root crop that tolerates poor soil and drought, providing food security between harvests.
actions: Plant stem cuttings 20–25 cm long, 1 m apart, at the start of the rains.
Weed during the first 3 months until the canopy closes.
Harvest roots from 9–12 months; leaves can be eaten as a vegetable.

sections.heading: Planting
sections.body: Use healthy stem cuttings 20–25 cm long from plants 8–12 months old. Plant at an angle, 1 m apart, when the rains begin.

sections.heading: Care and harvest
sections.body: Keep weed-free for the first 3 months. Harvest from 9 months; roots keep best if left in the ground and dug as needed.
